docClaim.quote: Buffers are taken into consideration while booking a Cal event, if that Cal event has a buffer time selected. ... When buffers are enabled, Cal.com treats that extra time as busy, so new bookings cannot overlap it. ... Every meeting creates a protected time window around it. ... Other meetings cannot be scheduled inside this protected window.

colleagueFinding.note: Does not map to any of caldiy #1 to #5 in /Users/musheghgevorgyan/repos/cal.diy/docs/guard-findings.md; none of the five concerns buffers (they are out-of-office, team slot length, date-override slot grid, seated oversell, unauthenticated hold control). It does fall squarely under the coordinator's already-established systemic cause 3, cross-scenario slot contention on reference-host, and it refines that cause with a worked example: the brief's parenthetical 'buffered event types lose 9:30am too' is confirmed here, and the mechanism is the queried event type's beforeEventBuffer padding the busy block, not anything about the buffered event type's own schedule.

notes: Why the product is in the clear, verified in the tested worktree rather than inferred. (1) packages/features/busyTimes/services/getBusyTimes.ts:132-179 pads every existing booking by minutesToBlockBeforeEvent = existingEventType.beforeEventBuffer + queriedEventType.afterEventBuffer and minutesToBlockAfterEvent = existingEventType.afterEventBuffer + queriedEventType.beforeEventBuffer (lines 135-136, applied at 177-178). seated-consult carries no buffer, buffered-consult carries 30 before and 30 after, so the 09:00-09:30 booking becomes busy 08:30-10:00 when the slots are computed for buffered-consult. That kills the 9:00 and 9:30 starts and leaves 10:00 free on the boundary, which is exactly the grid the page rendered. (2) The blocking booking is a SEATED one, and getBusyTimes.ts:140-167 only softens a seated booking to buffer-only busy time when eventTypeId === eventType?.id, so for any other event type the seat is full busy time. (3) BookingRepository.ts:686-745 (query one) selects every ACCEPTED booking of the user in the window with no eventTypeId filter, which is what makes one scenario's booking host-wide. Its query three, the PENDING one, IS eventTypeId-scoped (lines 759-775), which is why the notice-confirm scenario's requires-confirmation booking at the same 9:00 did not block anything here. (4) The day really does open at 09:00 for this event type, so the missing slots are busy time and not a narrower seeded window: buffered-a, the other 30-before/30-after event type on the same host, offers 9:00am as its first slot on its contention-free day (stacked-buffers-block-more-than-one-buffer-width.web.1, /reference-host/buffered-a?month=2027-03, passes), so a 30/30 buffer does not shave a schedule's own leading edge; and the five sibling event types on 2030-06-12 show the identical 12:00 window end with only the 09:00 start missing. Two further points for whoever owns the corpus. The failing step carries NO milestone, it is the baseline the real assertion is read against, so nothing was disproved: all six buffer milestones (buffers-are-considered-while-booking, buffers-subtract-time-around-a-meeting, buffer-time-is-treated-as-busy, each-meeting-has-a-protected-time-window, no-meeting-scheduled-inside-the-protected-window, buffers-cannot-overlap-cal-events) remain unproven because step 8 never ran. And the scenario was unsalvageable from step 2 onward anyway: step 8 requires 9:00am to be VISIBLE after its own 10:00 booking, and 9:00am had already been taken by the sibling. The irony worth reporting upward is that the failing evidence is itself a clean demonstration of the doc claim, an unbuffered event type lost only the booked 09:00 half-hour while the 30/30 buffered one lost 09:00 and 09:30, just measured against a baseline the scenario assumed instead of captured. Fix: give the buffer flow its own day or its own host the way stacked-buffers does with 2027-03-15 on buffered-a, or serialize the 2030-06-12 family, or make step 8 relative by diffing the grid captured at step 2 against the grid after the booking instead of hardcoding 9:00am and 9:30am. One observed wrinkle that does not change the verdict: at 03:50:08 the tz-locked page on the same day showed 9:00am, 9:30am, 10:30am, 11:00am, 11:30am, so a 10:00-10:30 booking existed on the host at that moment and was gone by 03:50:26 when this page loaded. The shared day's state moves under the scenarios throughout the run, which is the same contention problem seen from another angle.
